text:
Devon C: FYI noticed on-prem admin console started returning 403s after the RBAC refactor merged this morning. CLI also failing to list clusters.
Tess R: ugh, which refactor? the roles->policies flattening?
Devon C: yes, PR #4123 — flatten admin roles into cluster-admin-compat. rollout went to private control plane at 09:04 UTC.
Samir P: can you paste the exact error?
Devon C: `error: You must be permitted to perform action 'list' on 'clusters' (403)` when running `kubectl --context=onprem-admin get clusters`
Mira L: did the allowlist IP ranges change for the on-prem API? Could be VPC gating combined with a role mapping slip.
Devon C: I validated from our jumpbox (same IP) before/after — IP allowed. So sounds like RBAC mapping.
security-oncall (bot): Incident template created: INC-2024-089 — Suspected admin role regression on private control plane.
Samir P: pulling audit logs now. If anyone can run the quick impersonation check: `kubectl auth can-i --as system:serviceaccount:platform:svc-deploy list clusters`
Devon C: ran it -> `no`
Samir P: got logs snippet from control plane audit: `time=2024-07-25T09:05:13Z user="svc-deploy@platform" verb=list resource=clusters namespace=default outcome=Forbidden reason="RBAC: rolebinding mismatch"`
Devon C: interesting — looks like rolebinding for svc-deploy wasn't migrated to cluster-admin-compat. PR script maybe skipped cluster-scoped bindings.
Mira L: there are also KMS denied errors in the same time window (we rotate KMS grants when we recreate bindings). audit-bot, can you grep?
audit-bot: matched logs -> `2024-07-25T09:05:12Z KMS:EncryptDenied principal=svc-deploy@platform key=projects/rdw-prod/locations/global/keyRdr`
Tess R: if KMS encrypt/decrypt is denied, service tokens may fail to validate role certificates — could be cascading.
Samir P: timeline looks like: role refactor job ran -> rolebindings rewired -> KMS grant reconciliation job ran -> KMS grant failed due to missing service account in allowlist -> svc-deploy lost ability to decrypt cluster certs -> RBAC checks failed -> 403 surfaced.
Devon C: that matches. Where did the KMS allowlist come from? I thought KMS grants are project-level.
Mira L: we added a per-key allowlist last quarter for private deployments (key-level principal allowlist) — it only accepts principals explicitly enumerated. The role-migrate job creates new principals (new binding subjects) which weren't added to the key allowlist.
Tess R: ok action items: 1) revert or patch role-migrate to keep original subject names during migration OR update KMS allowlist; 2) create fallback that keeps old bindings active until grant reconciliation succeeds; 3) add automated can-i + KMS sanity check in rollout job.
Devon C: for short term I updated KMS allowlist to include svc-deploy@platform and re-ran reconciliation. Confirming... now `kubectl get clusters` succeeds from jumpbox.
security-oncall (bot): INC-2024-089 status -> mitigated (action: temporary KMS allowlist update).
Samir P: please open follow-up bug for the role-migrate script: `ENGSEC-2342` for root cause + tests for KMS interactions.
Mira L: I'll add an audit alert for any role-binding changes that remove cluster-scoped subjects without a matching KMS grant delta in the same change window.
Tess R: also suggesting we add a preflight that simulates `kubectl auth can-i --as` for a small set of service accounts and validates KMS decrypt on key. Sample snippet we can add to CI: ```bash
# preflight check (simulated)
for sa in svc-deploy svc-monitor; do
  kubectl auth can-i --as system:serviceaccount:platform:$sa list clusters || echo "RBAC fail: $sa"
  gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy keyRdr || echo "KMS unreachable"
  # attempt decrypt using service account token (short-lived simulation)
done
```
Devon C: sounds good. I'm going to keep the temporary allowlist change for a couple of hours while we push a migration patch.
Mira L: logging note — we should annotate the audit log when we do manual patches so post-incident reviews can correlate KMS allowlist edits with RBAC restores.
Devon C: added comment on INC-2024-089 with steps taken + KMS acl diff.
Samir P: anyone see a security escalation risk from the temporary allowlist addition? we added only three service accounts and limited it to the KMS key used by the control plane.
Tess R: low blast radius but we should rotate the grant back to least-priv once migration is complete and document the exception.
security-oncall (bot): Reminder: mark incident as "postmortem required" if it affected customer-facing private deployments.
Devon C: will start a short postmortem draft. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
